note: Real. Mike Evans (TB WR) broke his collarbone (and took a concussion) in the second quarter of the Week 7 Monday night loss at Detroit (Oct 20, 2025), his first game back from a hamstring strain that cost him Weeks 4-6. He had surgery and went on IR Oct 22. His ESPN 2025 game log shows Weeks 1-3 and 7, then Week 15 (Dec 11, TNF vs ATL, 6-132): group B, backWeek 15. The Bucs' bye was Week 9, so the second ask's week 9 is a bye week for him. Times are CBS page timestamps (RotoWire blurbs, one CBS Sports story) and Yardbarker's syndication of Pro Football Rumors (00:17 AM EDT Oct 21), which carries Bowles' postgame quote via Greg Auman and Jordan Schultz's 6-8 week report; I did not open Schultz's own X post or Auman's. ESPN's injury-night story (Jenna Laine) shows 00:53Z, which is before Bowles spoke postgame, so it was updated later and is left out.

news.source: RotoWire via CBS (citing Rick Stroud, Tampa Bay Times)
news.words: Evans will be sidelined for most of the year after suffering a broken collarbone in Monday's 24-9 loss to the Lions. Evans suffered the injury in the second quarter while attempting to reel in a deep target.

Evans will miss most of the remaining games on the Buccaneers' regular season schedule after breaking his collarbone, Tampa Bay coach Todd Bowles said following Monday night's loss. He was carted into the locker room.

news.source: Todd Bowles, postgame (via Greg Auman, FOX Sports; Pro Football Rumors on Yardbarker)
news.words: "He'll be out mostly toward the end of the year," Bowles told reporters. "We'll see what happens."

news.source: Jordan Schultz (via Pro Football Rumors on Yardbarker)
news.words: It sounds like Bowles may have been estimating the worst-case scenario. Jordan Schultz reports that the wideout's initial timeline is six to eight weeks, which would give him a couple of games before the playoffs.

news.source: RotoWire via CBS (citing Ian Rapoport, NFL Network; Todd Bowles via Scott Smith, Buccaneers.com)
news.words: Evans is scheduled to undergo surgery this week on a clean break, facing a recovery timetable of eight weeks or less. Bowles said Wednesday Evans will be "touch and go" to return before the regular season ends.

The Buccaneers placed Evans (collarbone) on injured reserve Wednesday. He's officially ruled out for the next four games, with surgery scheduled this week. The team has hope to get him back later this season.
